newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean freight forwarders complain at cash squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Korean freight forwarders complain at cash squeeze.

text.p: The president of the Korea International Freight Forwarders Association (KIFFA), J.M. Kim, said his members are being badly squeezed by airlines demanding a cash bond for carrying cargo and customers who delay payment.

The first president of the newly enlarged KIFFA, which only used to represent Korea's sea freight forwarders but which last year merged with the Korean Multimodal Transport Association to represent 643 air and sea freight forwarders said cash flow was one of the biggest problems facing the industry.

" The cash flow system of many freight fowarding companies here is terrible. Forwarders must put up a lot of money to pay a guaranteed cash bond to the airline, the Cargo Account Settlement System (CASS), then pay the airline within 30 days. But at the same time it is traditional to give credit and have to wait two or three months for payment from the shipper. Some never pay," Kim told Reuters in an interview.

"As president of the association I am saying to my members 'please stop this credit system' but because of the heavy competition in the industry it will be very difficult. Everyone says the system should change but no one wants to be the first. Forwarders are having a very hard time in the meantime," Kim said.
The number of Korean air freight forwarders had mushroomed because last year changes in the law allowed sea freight forwarders into the market, Kim said.
But while the amount of tonnage handled by Korea's freight forwarders had recently risen, revenue had fallen and the industry faced a difficult future, he added.
"Now it is a free for all and too many people are chasing a piece of the cake," Kim added.
